nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is a bijection.
nodes.title: The chosen linear extension is bijective

nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$, the number of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is positive.
nodes.title: The number of linear extensions is positive

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). This is the order isomorphism from $\alpha$ with that linear order onto $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ with its usual order.
nodes.title: Ranking a Szpilrajn linear extension

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. Its linear extensions are represented as rank functions: the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is the finite set of all maps $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that are bijective and monotone, meaning that $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.
nodes.title: Linear extensions of a finite poset

nodes.summary: For a finite subset $A$ of a partially ordered set $P$, the maximal elements of $A$ form the subset of those $x \in A$ such that every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.
nodes.title: Maximal elements of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. A map $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ belongs to the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ if and only if $\sigma$ is bijective and monotone.
nodes.title: Membership in the linear extensions

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite subset of a partially ordered set $P$ and let $x \in P$. Then $x$ belongs to the set of maximal elements of $A$ if and only if $x \in A$ and every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.
nodes.title: Membership in the maximal elements

nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is monotone: $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.
nodes.title: The chosen linear extension is monotone

nodes.summary: Every finite poset has a linear extension.
nodes.title: Existence of linear extensions

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). The chosen linear extension of $\alpha$ is the rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ sending each element to its position in that linear order, counted from $0$.
nodes.title: A chosen linear extension

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
